args: In PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/DnsLayer.cpp parseResources() and PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/DnsResource.cpp, what exact minimum fixed-field lengths must be available after a decoded DNS name before constructing/using DnsQuery versus DnsResource, and does any existing helper safely validate an encoded DNS name's on-wire length without constructing IDnsResource? Recommend the smallest robust root-cause patch.

The sanitizer crash occurs because parseResources starts each advertised record by constructing DnsQuery/DnsResource at offsetInPacket, even when offsetInPacket equals m_DataLen. IDnsResource's constructor immediately calls decodeName(getRawData()), and pointer arithmetic/read behavior reaches one byte beyond the packet. parseResources only compares offsetInPacket to m_DataLen after construction and getSize(). The malicious DNS counts total under the 300-record cap but exceed captured records. I am considering a precheck for at least the name-start byte and then checking query fixed fields (QTYPE/QCLASS) or resource fixed fields (TYPE/CLASS/TTL/RDLENGTH and RDATA) before accepting each object; I need to understand exact layouts and whether constructor/getSize can safely determine name length once the starting byte is in bounds.
